ban/0.text: Rulers kept trying to ban it. Coffeehouses, they said, were where sedition happened. The bans lasted, on average, one sultan.

conquest/0.text: Venice fell first. Then Paris, then London, then everywhere ships could reach. The most successful conquest in history required no army at all — just breakfast.

goats/0.text: Legend says coffee was discovered in Ethiopia by a goatherd named Kaldi, whose goats ate some red berries and refused to sleep. Ever.

trade/0.text: By the fifteenth century the beans had crossed the Red Sea to Yemen, and the port of Mocha was shipping caffeine to Istanbul and beyond.
